##################### 92930122 #####################
=== REAL JD ===
About the Role
We're looking for a Digital Project Manager to drive custom web application builds through to delivery. You won't be writing the code (we build with Next.js, Nuxt.js, Node.js, microservices and many others), and our MD and Business Analyst lead the upfront scoping. But from there the build is yours to own. You'll work alongside the client throughout delivery, helping them understand how the solution maps to their business and the value it unlocks, and you'll manage the work through to built, tested and shipped, on time and to spec. You'll also be a real voice in shaping it, spotting where something could work better or where there's a smarter way to connect the dots, and feeding that back into the build.
Just as importantly, you'll be the dedicated point of contact for clients. You'll understand the system well enough to talk them through how their data moves between platforms and where things connect, and you'll have the commercial sense to know when something's worth doing and when it isn't - we run true partnerships with our clients with projects evolving over many years. We're after someone who's been part of a custom web application build before and gets how the pieces fit together, not just websites.

Must Haves
• Web Application Delivery: You've worked on at least 3 custom web application build, not just websites or CMS sites. You understand how a build moves from tickets to delivery and how to keep it on track.

• Ticket-Driven Delivery: Comfortable picking up scoped requirements from a Business Analyst, coordinating developers, and managing work through testing, UAT and release.

• Technical Literacy (Conceptual): You can discuss APIs, databases, ERPs and CRMs at a conceptual level. You don't need to be an expert, but you understand what they are and how data flows between systems. Awareness of modern stacks (Next.js, Nuxt.js, microservices) is a plus.

• Client-Facing: You can sit with a client, connect the dots on their data and systems, and talk through where information moves from one place to another and what's possible.

• Commercial Acumen: You can weigh up whether a feature or integration is worth building, and you're confident saying "yes, that makes sense" or "there's no real return there" and explaining why.

• AI Native: Comfortable using AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT and similar platforms day-to-day to accelerate work, draft documentation, analyse problems and solve them. You're curious about where AI fits into how a modern software team delivers, and keen to push it further.

• Organisational Skills: Strong organisational skills to manage multiple projects and competing priorities efficiently.

• Client Communication: Excellent communication skills for working with clients and keeping them confident and informed through a build.

• Attention to Detail: A keen eye for detail across delivery and quality.

• Task Management Tools: Familiarity with ClickUp is a plus, but not mandatory. Being adaptable to similar tools is what matters.

About Us
Arcadian Digital is a Melbourne-based software and AI solutions partner. Since 2014 we've delivered production-grade web applications and embedded AI into the systems businesses actually run on. Strategy leads and technology follows, so every project is anchored to a real business outcome rather than tech for its own sake. We're a Claude partner, we use agentic AI deeply in our own delivery, and we work across industries including building supplies and trades, energy and utilities, logistics, mining, financial services and more, for clients like Bowens, Roy Morgan Research, CitiPower Powercor and Australia Post.
We're a small, senior team that values straight answers and doing the work properly. You'll be based at our Melbourne CBD office with a hybrid model, working on genuinely complex custom builds rather than templated websites. There's good coffee, a Friday drinks fridge and a lunch out together every Friday, but the real draw is the calibre of the work and the people you'll do it with.

Only successful applicants will be contacted for an interview.

●  A collaborative, innovative, and fun work environment – your Justice League awaits!
●  Boundless opportunities for professional growth and to level up your skills.
Ready to Join the League? (How to Apply):
If you're thrilled by the chance to shape the technology of the future and make a monumental impact at ThorAI Group, send us your resume and a cover letter.
Tell us about the products you’ve launched, your greatest strategic triumphs, and why you’re the Visionary we’re looking for!

# Cover-Letter Drafting Brief — Nick Wood application batch (2026-06-25)

You are drafting ONE tailored cover letter for ONE role. Read the role's JD file and the assigned CV variant file (paths given in your task). This brief holds the positioning rules. Follow them exactly.

## Who Nick is (one line)
T-shaped Melbourne software engineer (~7 yrs, senior/lead level: ANZ, Macquarie, Leidos) pivoting toward strategic/AI-leveraged work, with engineering depth as the differentiator. Not leaving engineering behind.

## Recurring proof points (use the ones that fit the role; never dump all)
- **ANZ Plus (Jan 2025–Mar 2026):** owned AI-enabled search APIs on a generative-AI search platform (Vertex AI / Gemini) in a 12-engineer team; drove AI integration strategy (model selection, provisioning, scaling); set practical GenAI guardrails in a regulated bank; Golang microservices, gRPC/Protobuf. Was on ANZ Plus's early Claude Code trial; agentic dev is how he works now.
- **Macquarie (Apr 2023–Jan 2025):** architected + led a 4-engineer team delivering a real-time, event-driven asset-management platform; cut manual effort 50+ hrs/week; GCP, Java/Spring Boot.
- **Leidos (Jul 2019–Apr 2023):** data discovery platform for a government agency (months → seconds); 2-person PoC that won a defence contract extension; dual-hat Scrum Master scaling 2→6 teams.
- **LIMSOC / Life Saving Victoria (Feb–Apr 2026, paid independent consult):** national scaling STRATEGY (NOT a national product) for a 199,000-member, $100M federated org; pulled SEVEN jurisdictions into one product operating model + roadmap; authored and presented strategy to C-suite, accepted as foundation for national adoption.
- **Water safety policy:** board-endorsed, adopted as a national standard.
- **AccessBuddy:** multi-tenant SaaS he shipped solo with AI-assisted dev; live with real users (NOT "paying"/"commercial"); first tenant ~190 members, 350+ credentials.
- Runs his own personal AI infrastructure (agents/automation) he built himself.

## HARD positioning rules (violating these fails the draft)
1. **Cover-letter structure: "what sets me apart → how I built it → why this role."** No filler opener. No domain-apology paragraph. No comparisons to other candidates. No abrupt ending.
2. **Every paragraph leads with PAID or PROFESSIONAL proof** (ANZ, Macquarie, Leidos, or the LIMSOC consulting strategy). **AccessBuddy may appear ONLY as a brief closing clause**, never the lead or first concrete proof of ANY paragraph. Example allowed closing clause: "Outside paid work I keep building, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I shipped solo."
3. **LIMSOC = scaling strategy, seven jurisdictions** (never "national product", never eight).
4. **AccessBuddy = solo/personal build, live with real users.** Never "paying", never "commercial", never headline it.
5. **BANNED phrasing** — never use "you are describing the work I already do" or any cousin ("this is the work I have been doing", "exactly the work I have been doing", "the role you describe is what I already do", "the work I have done for years"). State the capability directly instead.
6. **No em dashes. Australian English.** Exec-ready, confident, specific, varied rhythm. Paragraphs do the work, not bullet lists. Not formally corporate. Don't formalise away Nick's directness.
7. **No "non-traditional background" framing.** Engineering + strategy + founder-execution is a rare, valuable combination — that's the argument.
8. **Don't volunteer GPA.** Don't claim titles he doesn't hold (he is not a formal "Product Manager" or "people-manager"; he has done product-adjacent and lead-level work).
9. **Agile stance** (if relevant): believes in agile as a delivery approach but keeps it flexible to the company rather than by-the-book. Not a zealot, not anti-agile.
10. Salutation: "Dear Hiring Team," unless the JD names a person. Sign off:
    Nicholas Wood
    0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

## Voice exemplar (recent, approved — match this register, do not copy content)
> The thing I have found about AI in practice is that it changes what one person can do, and I have built my recent work around that. I was one of the leads developing the AI-enabled search APIs at ANZ Plus... What sets me apart is that I pair that engineering depth with a commercial and product head. I start with the business problem and its context, not the tool, then build the thing that actually creates value... My motivation has always been work with real impact.

## Length
~300–380 words. Four short paragraphs is the target shape. Tight.

## What to return (exactly this structure)
1. `## FIT ASSESSMENT` — 4-6 sentences: genuine strengths, genuine gaps/risks vs the JD (be honest — e.g. language stack mismatch, seniority/tenure screen, comp), and a recommendation (apply / apply-with-caveat / reconsider).
2. `## CV VARIANT` — confirm the assigned variant is right, or recommend switching and why.
3. `## COVER LETTER` — the full letter, ready to paste. Plain text, no markdown headings inside it.
4. `## RED FLAGS` — anything in your own draft a reviewer should check (filler risk, any rule you were unsure about).

At Leidos I was a dual-hat Scrum Master while also writing production code, learning how to break large work into increments a multi-team program could review and deploy without losing momentum. That experience sits directly behind my current practice: I write the tests and the documentation that genuinely help a team ship and maintain, not to gold-plate, but because I have been the engineer who inherits undocumented code at 2am and I know what that costs. The student outcome focus is exactly the kind of concrete north star that makes trade-off decisions clear.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

At ANZ Plus I moved into Golang microservices at bank scale: gRPC and Protobuf-first API contracts, Terraform-managed infrastructure, Kafka-backed event flows, and AI-enabled search APIs that have to perform at the query volumes financial services infrastructure demands. At Macquarie I defined the engineering standards adopted by the team, TDD disciplines, coverage thresholds, code-review culture, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation patterns, and coached engineers through them. At Leidos I scaled an agile engineering organisation from two to six scrum teams and defined the cross-team standards that held it together. That is the role I am after and the environment I do my best work in.

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is that I sit naturally at the intersection the role describes, technically fluent enough to define and configure API integrations and AI agent workflows, commercially minded enough to own the client relationship and drive net retained revenue. That combination is unusual because it is built over time rather than by title: seven years across ANZ, Macquarie, and Leidos have given me the engineering depth, and a sequence of strategic engagements have given me the commercial and stakeholder muscle.

At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative-AI platform, one of only two initiatives taking AI directly to customers across more than 100 bank AI projects. I drove model selection, scaling patterns, and guardrails in a regulated environment where getting it wrong had real consequences. At Macquarie I translated operational requirements directly from business stakeholders into the architecture of a real-time asset management platform, leading a four-engineer team through design to delivery and eliminating more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. Earlier this year I consulted independently to Life Saving Victoria, taking their state-based incident management platform through a national scaling strategy: I designed the operating model, defined commercial and governance structures, and presented to C-suite, with the work accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. That is the shape of the forward deployment role: enter the client environment, understand the real constraint, configure the solution, and leave it running.

The specific draw here is the product itself. A continuous-onboarding AI agent that closes the gap between signed contract and deployed value is a problem I find genuinely compelling, it is where most enterprise software value actually goes to die. I want to be in accounts from day one, doing the 30 to 60 day sprint work, and feeding what I learn at the coalface back to the product team. I work well in high-ambiguity environments: the Life Saving Victoria engagement had no playbook, I built one.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is that I have built production AI systems and I understand the business problem first. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform, running on Vertex AI and Gemini, inside a 12-engineer team at a regulated bank. That work was not a prototype, it was production infrastructure with real compliance constraints, and I drove the decisions on model selection, provisioning approach, scaling patterns, and the practical guardrails to make it reliable. Go microservices, gRPC, GCP. I have also run agentic workflows and AI automation in my own engineering practice for the past 18 months, which has reshaped how I think about what one person, or one team, can actually deliver.

The engineering background runs deeper than that one role. At Macquarie I defined the solution architecture for a real-time asset management platform, led a four-engineer team through design and delivery, and worked directly with business stakeholders to translate operational processes into system design, cutting more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. Before that, at Leidos, I built a data discovery platform for a critical government agency that took analyst tasks from months down to seconds. I know how to scope the real problem, make the architecture decision that holds, and get things shipped.

The client-facing side of this role is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement with Life Saving Victoria: a national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform used in real-time emergency operations, presented to executive leadership and accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. That work required me to translate operational complexity into product and platform decisions, hold credibility with both frontline operators and the C-suite, and push back on the framing when the stated problem was not the real one. It is the same instinct this role calls for: understand the client's real problem before touching the technology.

One honest note: my primary backend languages are Go and Java, with Python firmly in the toolkit. My LLM and GenAI production experience is genuine, and that applied AI side is where I am most confident I add value from day one. Outside paid work I keep building, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I shipped solo with real users.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is not that I can read a tech stack, it is that I have spent seven years sitting in the space where the business problem, the engineering decision, and the commercial case all converge. At Macquarie I defined requirements directly with business stakeholders and end users, then led a four-engineer team to build a real-time asset management platform from design through delivery, cutting over 50 hours of manual work per week. At ANZ I owned an AI-enabled search platform in a 12-engineer team, making model selection, scaling, and API architecture decisions while maintaining delivery cadence in a regulated environment. At Leidos I dual-hatted as Scrum Master and engineer, scaling delivery from two to six teams while remaining accountable for the technical quality of what shipped. Across all three, I was the person who translated the business requirement into engineering decisions and held both sides of that conversation.

I have also done the consulting variant of that work. Earlier this year I was engaged to define the scaling strategy for a 199,000-member, $100M federated organisation's incident management platform, pulling seven jurisdictions into one product operating model and presenting the strategy to C-suite stakeholders. A central part of that engagement was exactly the kind of commercial sense you describe: distinguishing what was worth building from what was scope creep, and being prepared to explain why clearly.

Arcadian's model, strategy first and technology following, with long-term client partnerships, is the model I believe in. I have used Claude daily for the past year, built personal agentic infrastructure on top of it, and was part of ANZ Plus's early Claude Code trial. The "AI native" criterion is not a checkbox for me, it is how I actually work. The fact that Arcadian is a Claude partner and is thinking seriously about where AI fits into software delivery makes this a straightforward conversation.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

In Nick's cover letters, never reference the job ad with constructions like "the intersection the role describes", "the commercial sense you describe", "the same instinct this role calls for", or "that is the shape of the X role". Articulate the actual capability or work verbatim instead.

**Why:** It reads lazy and presumptuous, same family as the already-banned "you are describing the work I already do". The reader has the JD; pointing back at it adds nothing. Naming the thing directly is stronger and more specific.

All six are staged and positioning-clean, and your "no role-pointing" rule is now saved so it carries to future drafts. Here's the batch for your review.

---

## Two decisions for you (everything else is ready)

**1. KICK — values call.** KICK is owned by the **Easygo/Stake group (gambling/iGaming)** — the same parent behind the Easygo role you parked on domain grounds in the 16 Jun batch. Technical fit is genuinely one of the strongest here (real-time, 4M concurrent, Go, event-driven, Kafka/K8s/Terraform — straight off your Macquarie/ANZ work), but **PHP is a listed core language and you don't have it**. I've drafted it ready to go *if* you decide the domain is acceptable. Your call before it's submitted.

**2. Thor AI — comp call.** PM role, genuine substance fit, but **$120–140k is ~30–40% below your engineering watermark**, the equity is early-stage/illiquid, and the "3–5 yrs PM title" line is a plausible resume-screen rejection. Apply-with-caveat. Worth deciding if the step-down is worth your time before you invest in a process.

## One fix before the PM roles go out
The **Hybrid and Consulting CVs say "8 jurisdictions" / "8 state bodies"** — should be **seven** (settled figure). This affects the 3 hybrid-CV roles (Arcadian, Thor, Real Time). The **Engineering CV is clean** (no count), so Opus/Contour/KICK are unaffected. I can't regenerate the CV cleanly — the markdown sources didn't migrate from your Mac (it's offline) and only the PDFs are in OneDrive. Options: recover the source over SSH when the Mac's up, or I reconstruct the Hybrid/Consulting CV markdown from the PDF text and re-export with the fix. Say the word.

## Triage + recommendations

| Role | Company | Comp | CV | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Senior Agentic SWE | Opus (recruiter) | $180–250k | Eng | **Apply — strong.** Dead-on AI/consultative-engineer fit. Honest Python-gap note in letter (you're Go/Java-first). |
| "Forward Deployed" Technical PM | via Real Time | $200–220k+ESOP | Hybrid | **Apply — strong.** The embedded engineer-consultant T-shape, well paid. Likely your bullseye. |
| Senior SWE | Contour Education | $160–180k | Eng | **Apply.** Go + full-stack + product-first scale-up. Stack edges (Prisma/SST/Supabase) are learn-on-job. |
| Digital Project Manager | Arcadian Digital | not listed | Hybrid | **Apply.** Claude-partner delivery shop, AI-native, client-facing. No salary listed — raise early. |
| Product Manager | Thor AI | $120–140k | Hybrid | **Apply-with-caveat** (comp + PM-title screen). |
| Senior SWE | KICK (Easygo) | n/a | Eng | **Hold for your call** (iGaming domain + PHP gap). |

Two SWE agents made stray web-search calls that I had to recover from, but all six final letters are clean. Full per-role fit assessments are in the agent outputs; cover letters staged at `workspace/career/artifacts/applications/2026/2026-06-25/<role>/cover-letter.md`.

## The six cover letters

**Opus — Senior Agentic SWE** (408w)
> Dear Hiring Team,
> What sets me apart is that I have built production AI systems and I understand the business problem first. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform, running on Vertex AI and Gemini, inside a 12-engineer team at a regulated bank. That work was not a prototype, it was production infrastructure with real compliance constraints, and I drove the decisions on model selection, provisioning approach, scaling patterns, and the practical guardrails to make it reliable. Go microservices, gRPC, GCP. I have also run agentic workflows and AI automation in my own engineering practice for the past 18 months, which has reshaped how I think about what one person, or one team, can actually deliver.
> The engineering background runs deeper than that one role. At Macquarie I defined the solution architecture for a real-time asset management platform, led a four-engineer team through design and delivery, and worked directly with business stakeholders to translate operational processes into system design, cutting more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. Before that, at Leidos, I built a data discovery platform for a critical government agency that took analyst tasks from months down to seconds. I know how to scope the real problem, make the architecture decision that holds, and get things shipped.
> The client-facing side of this role is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement with Life Saving Victoria: a national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform used in real-time emergency operations, presented to executive leadership and accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. That work required me to translate operational complexity into product and platform decisions, hold credibility with both frontline operators and the C-suite, and push back on the framing when the stated problem was not the real one. It is the same instinct: understand the client's real problem before touching the technology.
> One honest note: my primary backend languages are Go and Java, with Python firmly in the toolkit. My LLM and GenAI production experience is genuine, and that applied AI side is where I am most confident I add value from day one. Outside paid work I keep building, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I shipped solo with real users.
> I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.
> Nicholas Wood

**Real Time — "Forward Deployed" Technical PM** (348w)
> Dear Hiring Team,
> What sets me apart is that I sit naturally where the technical and the commercial meet, technically fluent enough to define and configure API integrations and AI agent workflows, commercially minded enough to own the client relationship and drive net retained revenue. That combination is unusual because it is built over time rather than by title: seven years across ANZ, Macquarie, and Leidos have given me the engineering depth, and a sequence of strategic engagements have given me the commercial and stakeholder muscle.
> At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative-AI platform, one of only two initiatives taking AI directly to customers across more than 100 bank AI projects. I drove model selection, scaling patterns, and guardrails in a regulated environment where getting it wrong had real consequences. At Macquarie I translated operational requirements directly from business stakeholders into the architecture of a real-time asset management platform, leading a four-engineer team through design to delivery and eliminating more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. Earlier this year I consulted independently to Life Saving Victoria, taking their state-based incident management platform through a national scaling strategy: I designed the operating model, defined commercial and governance structures, and presented to C-suite, with the work accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. That is the work I do best: enter the client environment, understand the real constraint, configure the solution, and leave it running.
> The specific draw here is the product itself. A continuous-onboarding AI agent that closes the gap between signed contract and deployed value is a problem I find genuinely compelling, it is where most enterprise software value actually goes to die. I want to be in accounts from day one, doing the 30 to 60 day sprint work, and feeding what I learn at the coalface back to the product team. I work well in high-ambiguity environments: the Life Saving Victoria engagement had no playbook, I built one.
> I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.
> Nicholas Wood

**Contour — Senior SWE** (388w)
> Dear Hiring Team,
> The thing that has made me useful across my career is that I start with the problem, not the tool. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the centre of a generative AI platform: Go microservices, Vertex AI and Gemini, gRPC, 80 percent plus test coverage enforced by TDD standards I set for a 12-engineer team. Before shipping a line I was working through model selection tradeoffs and scaling patterns with the team, because the technical decisions only made sense in that context. At Macquarie I did the same thing with a real-time asset management platform for trading operations: defined requirements directly with business stakeholders and end users, led a four-engineer team through architecture and delivery, and cut manual effort by over 50 hours a week. The test I applied at the start of every sprint was whether what we were building would actually change how the business operated. When it did not, we renegotiated scope.
> That product-first instinct is something I have had to build deliberately over time. At Leidos I was a dual-hat Scrum Master while also writing production code, learning how to break large work into increments a multi-team program could review and deploy without losing momentum. That experience sits directly behind my current practice: I write the tests and the documentation that genuinely help a team ship and maintain, not to gold-plate, but because I have been the engineer who inherits undocumented code at 2am and I know what that costs. Outside paid work I keep building, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I shipped solo with Next.js, Postgres, and Cloud Run, live with real users.
> Contour's engineering mandate is a natural fit for how I work. A senior engineer who owns features end-to-end, brings a point of view, pushes back when something does not make sense, and commits fully once a direction is set, that is the operating model I have been working in. I want to be in a product that matters, alongside engineers who hold each other to a high standard, working toward outcomes I can see in the world. The student outcome focus is exactly the kind of concrete north star that makes trade-off decisions clear.
> I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.
> Nicholas Wood

**Arcadian — Digital Project Manager** (331w)
> Dear Hiring Team,

================= 01 PD DECODE AND FIT =================
# PD Decode and Fit Map - Virgin Senior AI Engineer

How to use this doc: this turns the position description into a fit map so you know, before you walk in, where you are obviously strong, where you bridge from adjacent experience, and where the honest gaps are and how to handle them. Round 1 is run by Harry (engineer who started when Jaimyn did) and the engineering lead. Round 2, if you get there, is the Head of AI and possibly Jaimyn.

---

## The role in one line
Senior AI Engineer, CIO Division / AI team, Brisbane, reports to Head of AI, Level 2B, no direct reports. A hands-on applied-AI plus full-stack engineer who ships production AI systems and is trusted with the delivery realities: testing, evaluation, observability, safe rollout, and stakeholder communication. This is an individual-contributor senior role with mentoring expectations, not a management role.

## What Virgin actually wants (read between the lines)
The PD says it three times in different words: "recognising the realities of delivery, trade-offs and compromise", "what it takes to deliver production-ready solutions, including testing, evaluation and observability", "technical excellence while recognising the realities of delivery". They have been burned by, or are guarding against, people who can prototype with an LLM but cannot operate it in production. Your entire career is production engineering rigour in regulated, high-stakes environments. That is the centre of your fit. Lead with it.

---

## Fit map: requirement → your evidence → confidence

### Strong (claim directly, with receipts)
| PD requirement | Your evidence |
|---|---|
| 3+ years production-grade systems | 6.5 years, senior/lead, ANZ + Macquarie + Leidos |
| Hands-on with LLMs (RAG, tool/function calling) | ANZ Plus generative-AI search platform on Vertex AI/Gemini, you owned the search/retrieval APIs |
| Cross-functional delivery (Product, Eng, Security, Legal/Privacy, Ops) | Regulated banking at ANZ; defined requirements directly with business at Macquarie; seven-jurisdiction stakeholder alignment at SLSA |
| Safety/guardrails, responsible AI | Established generative-AI guardrails in a risk-averse banking context |
| Observability (metrics, logs, traces) | OpenTelemetry across ANZ, Macquarie, AccessBuddy; Sentry, Better Stack |
| Security & privacy (IAM, secrets, PII, auditability) | Regulated banking; Secure Code Warrior; AWS Solutions Architect; data discovery for a critical govt agency at Leidos |
| Software engineering best practice (testing, CI/CD, design reviews) | TDD with 80%+ coverage enforced at ANZ and Macquarie; GitHub Actions, Bitbucket Pipelines |
| Agile delivery, roadmap ownership, estimation, stakeholder comms | Scrum Master scaling 2→6 teams in SAFe; LIMSOC product ownership and roadmap; exec presentations |
| Communicate to non-technical / executive audiences | Authored and presented national strategy to executive leadership; C-suite presentations |
| AWS cloud concepts | AWS Solutions Architect Associate; AWS used at ANZ, Macquarie, Leidos |
| Mentoring junior engineers | Mentored juniors at Macquarie; coached teams as Scrum Master |
| React + TypeScript | Macquarie real-time portal, Leidos rewrite, AccessBuddy Next.js |

### Bridge (true, but you adapt from adjacent ground, say so confidently)
| PD requirement | How you bridge |
|---|---|
| Python as primary language | You have used Python (Macquarie, ANZ stack) but Go and Java are your deepest. Bridge: strong polyglot, fluent in Python, and you reason about it from a deep systems base. See the senior-Python doc. Do not oversell, do not apologise. |
| FastAPI / FastMCP | Not used in production. Bridge: you know API design deeply (gRPC/Protobuf/REST, Google AIP standards at ANZ), FastAPI is a clean Python framing of the same concerns, and MCP is the protocol behind Virgin's own ChatGPT app. You have clearly done the reading. See the FastAPI/FastMCP doc and the ChatGPT Apps doc. |
| Advanced RAG | You built the retrieval side of a real RAG platform. Bridge: you have lived the core (retrieval quality, grounding, guardrails); the "advanced" techniques (re-ranking, hybrid, agentic RAG) you can discuss fluently. See the AI fundamentals doc. |
| Agentic systems (planning, memory) | You drove AI integration strategy and guardrails; agents are the next step. Bridge: you understand the loop, the risks, and the constraint-first design philosophy. |
| AWS (vs your GCP depth) | Your hands-on cloud depth is GCP (Cloud Run, Spanner, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, BigQuery). Bridge: AWS Solutions Architect certified, AWS used across roles, and cloud concepts transfer; you map GCP service to AWS equivalent comfortably (Cloud Run≈ECS/Fargate/App Runner, Pub/Sub≈SNS/SQS/EventBridge, BigQuery≈Redshift/Athena, Spanner≈Aurora/DynamoDB). |

### Honest gaps (do not hide, handle cleanly)
| Gap | Handling |
|---|---|
| Databricks (MLflow / Mosaic AI) | You have not used it. It is a desirable, not essential. Honest line: "I have not worked in Databricks specifically, I have worked across the GCP data stack, BigQuery, Dataflow, Spanner. I understand the lakehouse pattern and MLflow's role as a model registry and experiment tracker, and picking up a managed platform is not where I see risk." Then pivot to the transferable concept (registries, experiment tracking, automated evals) which you do understand. |
| pgvector / AWS Cognitive Search specifically | Concept is solid (you run Postgres, you understand vector search and ANN). You have not used pgvector in anger. Say the concept clearly and be honest you have not shipped on it. |
| Airline/travel domain | Desirable, not essential. You have zero airline experience and should not pretend otherwise. Counter-weight: you have deep regulated, safety-critical, real-time operational domain experience (banking, plus literal coastal emergency operations through LIMSOC). The mental model of safety-critical, real-time, high-consequence systems transfers; the domain specifics you would learn fast. |
| LangGraph / LangChain | Desirable. Know what they are (LangChain = LLM app framework/abstractions; LangGraph = graph/state-machine for controllable agent flows). Honest: you have read on them and understand the orchestration problem they solve, you have not built production on them. |

---

## The narrative spine for this interview (your layered story)
This is the exact thing the BCG post-mortem flagged: have a 90-second headline and pre-built 2-3 minute expansions per beat so "expand on the second pass" is mechanical.

**Headline (90 sec):** "I am a senior engineer who has spent the last few years on production AI in regulated environments. At ANZ Plus I owned the search APIs inside a generative-AI search platform on Vertex AI and Gemini, drove the AI integration strategy for the team, and put guardrails around generative AI in a context where a wrong answer has compliance consequences. Before that I architected a real-time asset platform at Macquarie. Alongside that I have built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS solo, so I have full-stack and operational ownership end to end. What I care about is the gap between an AI demo and a production AI system, retrieval quality, evaluation, guardrails, observability, and I bring the testing and operational discipline that closes it."

**Expansion beats (each 2-3 min, have a concrete scene ready):**
1. The ANZ RAG/search platform: what it did, your piece, the model-selection and scaling decisions, the guardrails.
2. Guardrails in a regulated context: a specific control you put in and why.
3. Macquarie real-time platform: architecture decision, the event-driven design, the 50-hours-a-week saved.
4. AccessBuddy: full-stack solo ownership, the operational side (observability, CI/CD), why it proves breadth not just a side project.
5. Stakeholder/exec communication: the LIMSOC national strategy presented to executive leadership, seven-jurisdiction alignment.

---

## Questions to ask them (signals seniority and genuine interest)
- "Where is the AI team on the build-vs-buy line, how much is building on foundation models and orchestration versus training/fine-tuning your own?"
- "The flight-search app in ChatGPT is live, what is the architecture behind it, and what is the roadmap, partner airlines and international were mentioned publicly?" (shows you did the homework, ties to MCP)
- "How mature is the eval and LLMOps tooling today, and where do you most want to lift it?" (signals you think about the production realities they emphasised)
- "How is the AI team set up relative to Data Science and Platform Engineering, where are the boundaries?"
- "What does the first six months look like for someone in this role, what would success be?"
- For the Head of AI in round 2: "What is your thesis on where AI gives Virgin the most leverage, customer experience, operations, or revenue/loyalty?" (the PD names all three)

---

## Tone reminders (from your standing positioning rules)
- Recommendation first, then reasoning. No sycophancy.
- Australian English, no em dashes, direct.
- AccessBuddy is supplementary proof, a personal full-stack build that proves breadth and operational ownership, never the headline. For this engineering AI role it is allowed as a genuine engineering example, but ANZ and Macquarie lead.
- Do not volunteer GPA. Address only if asked.
- Do not use "this is exactly the work I already do" constructions. State the capability directly.
- It is fine and good to say "I have not used X" cleanly and pivot to the transferable concept. Honesty plus a strong bridge reads as senior. Bluffing reads as junior, and Jaimyn warned the questions are pointed enough to expose a bluff.

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is that I have already taken AI to customers in production, not in a demo. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform on Vertex AI and Gemini. It was one of only two initiatives, out of more than 100 AI projects across the bank, that put AI directly in front of customers, and I drove the decisions that made it safe to ship: model selection, retrieval quality, scaling patterns, and the guardrails a regulated bank needs before a generative system ever reaches a real person. The engineering underneath that is genuine. Most recently I built AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I designed, built, and deployed solo, live with real users.

The client-facing side of this work is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement for Life Saving Victoria, defining the national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform and presenting it to executive leadership, accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. I am comfortable sitting with a client, finding the real problem behind the stated one, and designing the system that solves it.

One honest note: my deepest backend languages are Go and Java, with Python firmly in the toolkit. My LLM and GenAI production experience is the real differentiator, and the applied AI side is where I am most confident I add value from day one.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

I am a software engineer with an entrepreneurial mindset and real product experience, and this is the role I want to grow into. I am making a deliberate move from building systems to owning the commercial and product outcome at the coalface, and I think you are exactly the kind of team to make that move with. I will be upfront that I have not held the title of forward-deployed PM before. I am asking you to take a chance on that, because I am confident about what happens when you do.

Here is what you would be backing. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform and led the team that delivered it. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to the C-suite as the foundation for national adoption. On the side I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product, so I know what it is to own something end to end and make it pay.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold the room with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

I know I am an unusual candidate for this. I also know I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in a room with you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, no hard feelings. I do not think that is how it will go. The version of this where you take the chance ends with clients who are genuinely blown away, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

Most senior engineers you talk to will understand your stack. Very few will also understand your domain from the inside. I do. I hold a Certificate IV in Training and Assessment, I have taught, and I have built training curriculum from scratch, designing how material is sequenced, where students get stuck, and what actually moves someone from confused to confident. When your product decisions come down to what genuinely helps a student learn, I am not guessing. That is the difference between building features and building the right features, and it is where I will deliver outsized value for Contour.

The engineering is senior and hands-on. At ANZ Plus I owned AI-enabled search APIs at the centre of a generative AI platform: Go microservices, gRPC, 80 percent plus test coverage on TDD standards I set for a 12-engineer team. At Macquarie I defined the architecture for a real-time platform and led a four-engineer team through delivery, working backward from what the business and its users actually needed before writing a line. I ship full-stack, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I built and deployed solo on Next.js, Postgres, and Cloud Run, live with real users. I am comfortable across your stack and quick to pick up the parts of it I have not used in anger.

The way you describe the role is the way I already work: own features end to end, stay close to the student outcome, bring a point of view, push back when something does not make sense, and commit fully once a direction is set. I break large work into increments a team can review and deploy, and I write the tests and docs that genuinely help people ship, not gold-plating while students wait.

An engineer who can build at a senior level and also reason about pedagogy and the student journey is rare. For a company whose whole reason to exist is putting the student first, that combination is not a nice-to-have, it is leverage. I would love to bring it to Contour.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

Most senior engineers you talk to will understand your stack. Very few will also understand your domain from the inside. I do. I hold a Certificate IV in Training and Assessment, I have taught, and I have built training curriculum from scratch, designing how material is sequenced, where students get stuck, and what actually moves someone from confused to confident. When your product decisions come down to what genuinely helps a student learn, I am not guessing. That is the difference between building features and building the right features, and it is where I will deliver outsized value for Contour.

The engineering is senior and hands-on. At ANZ Plus I owned AI-enabled search APIs at the centre of a generative AI platform: Go microservices, gRPC, 80 percent plus test coverage on TDD standards I set for a 12-engineer team. At Macquarie I defined the architecture for a real-time platform and led a four-engineer team through delivery, working backward from what the business and its users actually needed before writing a line. I ship full-stack, most recently AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I built and deployed solo on Next.js, Postgres, and Cloud Run, live with real users. I am comfortable across your stack and quick to pick up the parts of it I have not used in anger.

The way you describe the role is the way I already work: own features end to end, stay close to the student outcome, bring a point of view, push back when something does not make sense, and commit fully once a direction is set. I break large work into increments a team can review and deploy, and I write the tests and docs that genuinely help people ship, not gold-plating while students wait.

An engineer who can build at a senior level and also reason about pedagogy and the student journey is rare. For a company whose whole reason to exist is putting the student first, that combination is not a nice-to-have, it is leverage. I would love to bring it to Contour.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

I am an engineer who has spent the last few years moving deliberately toward product and delivery ownership, and a Digital Project Manager at a Claude-partner agency that takes complex custom builds seriously is the logical next step. I want to make this move, and I think Arcadian is the right place to make it. What you would be getting is rare: one person who can own a build technically, manage it to delivery, hold the client relationship, and make the commercial calls along the way.

The technical credibility is genuine. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I use Claude and agentic tooling every day, built my own AI infrastructure on top of it, and was on ANZ Plus's early Claude Code trial, so the way Arcadian delivers is the way I already work. Across my career I have not just written code, I have worked as architect, Scrum Master, and business analyst through dual-hat roles and secondments, which is exactly the range a delivery owner needs to read a build, coordinate developers, and talk to a client about how their data moves between systems.

The product and delivery experience is just as real. Earlier this year I ran an independent consulting engagement for Life Saving Victoria, defining the product operating model and roadmap and presenting the strategy to the C-suite. I have acted as de facto product manager for national volunteer organisations, and I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product. I have made the commercial judgement this role calls for many times: deciding what is worth building, what is scope creep, and being able to explain why.

So I will be direct. Give me a project and you will not have to think about it again. I am confident it will not take long to build that confidence in me. I know I am a strong fit, and I am asking you to take the chance, because I am sure of how it ends. If we meet and you see it differently, that is a fair outcome. I do not expect it.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

The hard part of AI in financial services is never the model, it is knowing which problem to aim it at and earning the trust of the engineers, data scientists, and compliance people who each see that problem differently. I have done it in production. At ANZ Plus I owned one of only two initiatives, out of more than 100 AI projects across the bank, that took AI directly to customers. I set the product direction for our AI-enabled search platform, drove model selection, scaling, and guardrails in a regulated environment, and kept a 12-engineer cross-functional team aligned. The work shipped, and I learned exactly what it takes to make AI safe and useful in front of real users.

What I offer a company at your stage is range. In a small team the people who matter are the ones who can move across roles and lift whichever one needs lifting, and that is how I work. Across my career I have been a software engineer, a solution architect, a business analyst, and a Scrum Master, and alongside that I have run product and strategy: a national platform operating model and roadmap for a 199,000-member organisation, presented to the C-suite, and AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I designed, built, and shipped solo. I can talk architecture with your data scientists in the morning and translate the same work for a client's executive team in the afternoon, and I do not need a handover between the two.

ThorAI is solving a real problem: financial institutions with genuine AI ambition and a gap between what the technology can do and what they can bring to market. I understand that gap from inside a regulated bank, from the engineering bench, and from a strategy engagement that had to survive the jump from concept to executive sign-off. That is the work I want to be doing, and I would do it well here.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

input.content:
Dear Hiring Team,

Maintaining consistent low-latency chat, real-time viewer state, and platform stability across millions of concurrent sessions is a class of problem I have spent the last three years building for in production. At Macquarie I designed and led the delivery of a high-throughput, low-latency event-driven platform inside the trading and asset management division: event-sourced architecture on GCP, Kubernetes, and Pub/Sub, with full OpenTelemetry instrumentation and a four-engineer team to bring it across the line. The constraint was not just throughput, it was regulatory traceability under load, which means reliability and observability cannot be afterthoughts. That system replaced more than 50 hours of manual operational effort per week and passed architecture review. At ANZ Plus I moved into Golang microservices at bank scale: gRPC and Protobuf-first API contracts, Terraform-managed infrastructure, Kafka-backed event flows, and AI-enabled search APIs built to perform at the query volumes financial services infrastructure demands. I set and enforced an 80 percent test coverage standard and instrumented distributed tracing across the service mesh, because performance without observability is just luck.

Beyond the code, I bring the standards-setting and mentoring the role calls for. At Macquarie I defined the engineering standards the team adopted, TDD disciplines, coverage thresholds, code-review culture, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation patterns, and coached engineers through them. At Leidos I scaled an agile engineering organisation from two to six teams and defined the cross-team standards that held it together. These are how I have operated at senior level across every role, not soft skills tacked onto a technical resume.

KICK is at a genuine inflection point: a globally distributed real-time platform whose architecture has to evolve while it runs, migrating toward high-performance Golang services. That is precisely where a senior engineer who has built at this layer, understands what breaks under concurrency and load, and sets the standards a broader team can rally around makes the most difference. That is the role I am after and the environment in which I do my best work.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

You can hand me a custom build and stop thinking about it. It will get delivered, the client will stay confident, and you will not wait long to trust me with the next one. That is the bet I want you to make, and I am deliberately direct about it because I know how well I fit what Arcadian does.

The foundation is rare in one person. I have spent seven years as a software engineer, and across that time I have also worked as a solution architect, a Scrum Master, and a business analyst through dual-hat roles and secondments, so I understand a custom build from scoping through tickets to release from every seat at the table. At ANZ Plus I owned AI-enabled search APIs, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers, so I know what production-grade AI actually requires, not just what a demo shows. I use Claude every day, build my own agentic automation, and was on ANZ Plus's early Claude Code trial, which is the same ground Arcadian works on as a Claude partner.

On top of the engineering I bring real product experience. I directed a national platform strategy for a 199,000-member, $100M organisation, owning the operating model, roadmap, and commercials and presenting to the C-suite. I act as the de facto product manager for Life Saving Victoria's communications systems, and I built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS, AccessBuddy, solo from problem to live product. I can sit with a client, map how their data moves between systems, and tell them honestly when something is worth building and when it is not.

I am at the point of making a deliberate move from pure engineering into delivery and product leadership, and this role is the logical next step. I know I am a strong fit. I am asking you to take the chance, and if you meet me and disagree, I will accept that. I am confident you will not.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

I am a software engineer with an entrepreneurial mindset and real product experience, and this is the role I want to grow into. I am making a deliberate move from building systems to owning the commercial and product outcome at the coalface, and I think you are exactly the kind of team to make that move with. I will be upfront that I have not held the title of forward-deployed PM before. I am asking you to take a chance on that, because I am confident about what happens when you do.

Here is what you would be backing. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform and led the team that delivered it. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to the C-suite as the foundation for national adoption. On the side I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product, so I know what it is to own something end to end and make it pay.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold the room with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

I know I am an unusual candidate for this. I also know I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in a room with you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, no hard feelings. I do not think that is how it will go. The version of this where you take the chance ends with clients who are genuinely blown away, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is that I have already taken AI to customers in production, not in a demo. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform on Vertex AI and Gemini. It was one of only two initiatives, out of more than 100 AI projects across the bank, that put AI directly in front of customers, and I drove the decisions that made it safe to ship: model selection, retrieval quality, scaling patterns, and the guardrails a regulated bank needs before a generative system ever reaches a real person. The gap between an AI demo and a production AI system, evaluation, grounding, guardrails, observability, is where I have spent the last few years, and it is the gap most teams underestimate.

The engineering underneath that is genuine. I architected Golang microservices and gRPC API contracts at ANZ, and before that designed and led delivery of a real-time, event-driven asset management platform at Macquarie, working directly with business stakeholders to translate operational processes into system design and cutting more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. I have also run agentic workflows and AI automation in my own engineering practice for the past 18 months, which has changed how I think about what one engineer can ship. Most recently I built AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS I designed, built, and deployed solo, live with real users.

The client-facing side of this work is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement for Life Saving Victoria, defining the national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform and presenting it to executive leadership, accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. I am comfortable sitting with a client, finding the real problem behind the stated one, and designing the system that solves it.

One honest note: my deepest backend languages are Go and Java, with Python firmly in the toolkit. My LLM and GenAI production experience is the real differentiator, and the applied AI side is where I am most confident I add value from day one.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

I am a software engineer with an entrepreneurial mindset and real product experience, and this is the role I want to grow into. I am making a deliberate move from building systems to owning the commercial and product outcome directly with the client, and I think you are exactly the kind of team to make that move with. I will be upfront that I have not held the title of forward-deployed PM before. I am asking you to take a chance on that, because I am confident about what happens when you do.

Here is what you would be backing. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform and led the team that delivered it. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to the C-suite as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am a software engineer with an entrepreneurial mindset and real product experience, and this is the role I want to grow into. I am making a deliberate move from building systems to owning the commercial and product outcome directly with the client, and I think you are exactly the kind of team to make that move with. I will be upfront that I have not held the title of forward-deployed PM before. I am asking you to take a chance on that, because I am confident about what happens when you do.

Here is what you would be backing. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform and led the team that delivered it. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to the C-suite as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

I know I am an unusual candidate for this. I also know I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in front of you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, that is fair. I do not think that is how it will go. The version where you take the chance ends with clients who are delighted with what we deliver, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

I am an engineer who has worked across product, delivery, and stakeholder engagement. Through my own engagements I have built a far broader skill set than the title suggests, and I want to bring it into my next role with expanded scope. A forward-deployed role that sits inside the client's business and owns the commercial outcome is where that breadth pays off, and you are exactly the kind of team I want to do it with.

Every part of what this role needs, I have already done somewhere demanding. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform and led the team that delivered it. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to the C-suite as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped AccessBuddy, a multi-tenant SaaS, solo, from problem to live product, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

I know I am an unusual candidate for this. I also know I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in front of you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, that is fair. I do not think that is how it will go. The version where you take the chance ends with clients who are delighted with what we deliver, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

You can hand me a custom build and not need to think about it again. It will get delivered, the client will stay confident, and you will not wait long to trust me with the next one. That is the bet I want you to make, and I am deliberately direct about it because I know how well I fit what Arcadian does.

The foundation is rare in one person. I have spent seven years as a software engineer, and across that time I have also worked as a solution architect, a Scrum Master, and a business analyst through dual-hat roles and secondments, so I understand a custom build from scoping through tickets to release from every seat at the table. At ANZ Plus I owned AI-enabled search APIs, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers, so I know what production-grade AI actually requires, not just what a demo shows. I use Claude every day, build my own agentic automation, and was on ANZ Plus's early Claude Code trial, which is the same ground Arcadian works on as a Claude partner.

On top of the engineering I bring real product experience. I directed a national platform strategy for a 199,000-member, $100M organisation, owning the operating model, roadmap, and commercials and presenting to the C-suite. I act as the de facto product manager for Life Saving Victoria's communications systems, and I built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS, AccessBuddy, solo from problem to live product. I can sit with a client, map how their data moves between systems, and tell them honestly when something is worth building and when it is not.

I am at the point of making a deliberate move from pure engineering into delivery and product leadership, and this role is the logical next step. I know I am a strong fit. I am asking you to take the chance, and if you meet me and disagree, I will accept that. I am confident you will not.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

I hold a Certificate IV in Training and Assessment, I have taught, and I have built training curriculum from scratch, designing how material is sequenced, where students get stuck, and what actually moves someone from confused to confident. Dear Hiring Team,

I am an engineer who has worked across product, delivery, and stakeholder engagement. Through my own engagements I have built a far broader skill set than the title suggests, and I want to bring it into my next role with expanded scope. A forward-deployed role that sits inside the client's business and owns the commercial outcome is where that breadth pays off, and you are exactly the kind of team I want to do it with.

Every part of what this role needs, I have already done somewhere demanding. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform, led the team that delivered it, and cut more than 50 hours of manual effort a week. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to national executives as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS solo, replacing thousands of manual emails and hundreds of hours of admin a year, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes the 30 to 60 day implementation sprint work. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

I know I am an unusual candidate for this. I also know I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in front of you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, that is fair. I do not think that is how it will go. The version where you take the chance ends with clients who are delighted with what we deliver, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

═══════ REAL TIME (final) ═══════
Dear Hiring Team,

I am an engineer who has worked across product, delivery, and stakeholder engagement. Through my own engagements I have built a far broader skill set than the title suggests, and I want to bring it into my next role with expanded scope. A forward-deployed role that sits inside the client's business and owns the commercial outcome is where that breadth pays off, and you are exactly the kind of team I want to do it with.

Every part of what this role needs, I have already done somewhere demanding. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects that took AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform, led the team that delivered it, and cut more than 50 hours of manual effort a week. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to national executives as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS solo, replacing thousands of manual emails and hundreds of hours of admin a year, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes a 30 to 60 day implementation sprint possible, and repeatable. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

My atypical background is exactly what turns a good delivery into a great one: the instinct to foresee the extra problem, solve it before it lands, and leave the client happier than they expected. I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in front of you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, that is fair. I do not think that is how it will go. The version where you take the chance ends with clients who are delighted with what we deliver, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is that I have already taken AI to customers in production, not in a demo. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform on Vertex AI and Gemini. It was one of only two initiatives, out of more than 100 AI projects across the bank, that put AI directly in front of customers, and I drove the decisions that made it safe to ship: model selection, retrieval quality, scaling patterns, and the guardrails a regulated bank needs before a generative system ever reaches a real person. The gap between an AI demo and a production AI system, evaluation, grounding, guardrails, observability, is where I have spent the last few years, and it is the gap most teams underestimate.

The engineering underneath that is genuine. I architected Golang microservices and gRPC API contracts at ANZ, and before that designed and led delivery of a real-time, event-driven asset management platform at Macquarie, working directly with business stakeholders to translate operational processes into system design and cutting more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. I also build agentic workflows and AI automation across my own projects and not-for-profit work, designing, building, and shipping them end to end, which has changed how I think about what one engineer can deliver.

The client-facing side of this work is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement for Life Saving Victoria, defining the national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform and presenting it to executive leadership, accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. I am comfortable sitting with a client, finding the real problem behind the stated one, and designing the system that solves it.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Team,

What sets me apart is the production engineering rigour I bring to AI, not demos. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs at the core of a generative AI search platform on Vertex AI and Gemini. It was one of only two initiatives, out of more than 100 AI projects across the bank, built to take AI directly to customers, and I drove the decisions that make that kind of system safe to ship: model selection, retrieval quality, scaling patterns, and the guardrails a regulated bank requires before a generative system can go in front of a customer. The gap between an AI demo and a production AI system, evaluation, grounding, guardrails, observability, is where I have spent the last few years, and it is the gap most teams underestimate.

The engineering underneath that is genuine. I architected Golang microservices and gRPC API contracts at ANZ, and before that designed and led delivery of a real-time, event-driven asset management platform at Macquarie, working directly with business stakeholders to translate operational processes into system design and cutting more than 50 hours of manual effort per week. I also build agentic workflows and AI automation across my own projects and not-for-profit work, designing, building, and shipping them end to end, which has changed how I think about what one engineer can deliver.

The client-facing side of this work is where my broader experience adds something. Earlier this year I ran a paid independent consulting engagement for Life Saving Victoria, defining the national scaling strategy for a mission-critical incident management platform and presenting it to executive leadership, accepted as the foundation for national adoption across seven jurisdictions. I am comfortable sitting with a client, finding the real problem behind the stated one, and designing the system that solves it.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood

Dear Hiring Team,

I am an engineer who has worked across product, delivery, and stakeholder engagement. Through my own engagements I have built a far broader skill set than the title suggests, and I want to bring it into my next role with expanded scope. A forward-deployed role that sits inside the client's business and owns the commercial outcome is where that breadth pays off, and you are exactly the kind of team I want to do it with.

Every part of what this role needs, I have already done somewhere demanding. At ANZ Plus I owned the AI-enabled search APIs on a generative AI platform, one of only two initiatives across more than 100 bank AI projects built to take AI directly to customers. I am fluent enough in API integrations, webhooks, and agent workflows to configure your product into a client's architecture myself, not hand it to someone else. At Macquarie I translated business requirements directly into a real-time platform, led the team that delivered it, and cut more than 50 hours of manual effort a week. Earlier this year I consulted independently for Life Saving Victoria, walking into a complex organisation with no playbook, finding the real problem, designing the operating model and commercials, and presenting it to national executives as the foundation for national adoption. Alongside that I built and shipped a multi-tenant SaaS solo, replacing thousands of manual emails and hundreds of hours of admin a year, so I know what it takes to own something end to end and make it commercially real.

That combination, an engineer who can sit inside a client's stack, a builder who has shipped his own product, and an operator who can hold credibility with executives, is what makes a 30 to 60 day implementation sprint possible, and repeatable. I want to be in the accounts from day one, drive adoption, and feed what I learn back to the product.

My atypical background is exactly what turns a good delivery into a great one: the instinct to foresee the extra problem, solve it before it lands, and leave the client happier than they expected. I am a strong fit, and I would back myself in front of you to prove it. If we meet and you do not agree, that is fair. I do not think that is how it will go. The version where you take the chance ends with clients who are delighted with what we deliver, and me having grown into one of the best hires you made.

I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the role further.

Nicholas Wood
0427 081 551 | nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com
